title: Quickpatch SDK developer sprint notes
content:
Context:
This is a compact, pragmatic sprint notebook for a 1-week "quickpatch" focused on raising first-time success for new SDK users during demos and paid trials. The idea: ship a small set of lab-ready fixes and content that unblock the top-5 immediate failure modes we see in the funnel (signup->first-API-call->first-embed->first-chat).

Sprint goals (measurable):
- Reduce time-to-first-success (TTFS) from sign-up to a verified API call in the sandbox by 30% (target median 7 minutes -> 5 minutes).
- Fix 3 reproducible crash/telemetry gaps in the local dev flow (errors that produce no helpful message).
- Add 2 micro-labs to the quickstart suite that map to real customer questions (embeddings search + streaming chat w/ fallback).

Audience: new devs, integrators running quick prototypes, SEs doing onsite demos. These notes are purposely terse — usable as a runbook for pair-programming.

Priority list (top issues observed from support + analytics):
1) Missing credential mismatch message: incorrect key -> 401 but no guidance. (Observed in sandbox logs: 34% of first-failed calls)
2) Local env mismatch (node version / missing TLS CA) -> cryptic socket errors. (12%)
3) Streaming partial-response handling: sample code doesn't show reconnect/fallback.
4) Embeddings schema mismatch in sample app: wrong vector length assumption causing downstream NPEs.
5) Telemetry gap: SDK swallow-on-error in stubbed mode — no event emitted to Sentry/GA.

Quick fixes to ship this sprint (owners and acceptance):
- DEVEX-178: Add explicit error mapping for 401/403 in client and a one-liner remediation message (owner: Priya). Acceptance: unit test + e2e in sandbox that shows the new message in UI and logs.
- GH #2389: update README examples to include CA/TLS troubleshooting steps and node engine rc. (owner: Ethan). Acceptance: local dev checklist executes on mac/linux in <3 steps.
- Streaming lab: create a small demo showing how to gracefully fall back to short-polling when a stream disconnects (owner: Samir). Acceptance: manual test that simulates stream drop and verifies message continuity.
- Embedding sample fix: update sample app types and add vector-length assert + doc note (owner: Maya). Acceptance: CI test that runs sample and asserts vector length.
- Telemetry: ensure SDK emits a "first_call_failed" event with error code for sandbox mode (owner: Priya). Acceptance: instrumented run captured by staging Sentry.

Micro-labs to author (deliverables):
A) embeddings-quick-lab.md (5–8 steps, includes common pitfalls and a tiny dataset).
B) stream-fallback-lab.md (walkthrough + network throttling recipe).
C) checklist.md: "first 7 minutes" for SEs doing a demo (copyable script).

Safety/PII considerations:
- Labs must not include real customer text. Use synthetic prompts with clear disclaimers.
- Sandbox keys must be rotation-safe and auto-expire; ensure lab steps demonstrate how to revoke test keys.

Telemetry & metrics to watch (how we know we succeeded):
- Funnel event: sandbox_signup -> sandbox_first_call_success (instrument a new conversion event).
- Support tickets tagged "first_call_error" should drop by 25% week-over-week after deploy.
- Median TTFS from session start measured via instrumented quickstart page.

Rollout plan (fast path):
- Day 0 (mon): land small client-side changes (error mapping + readme edits) as patch releases.
- Day 1 (tue): add lab markdown + CI smoke tests.
- Day 2 (wed): merge streaming lab demo + sample app fixes.
- Day 3 (thu): QA in sandbox + sign-off from SEs + update quickstart page.
- Day 4 (fri): release and monitor for regressions. If anything high-severity found, roll back incremental change.

Open questions / risks:
- How much of TTFS pain comes from UX vs infra (redirect loops in sign-up)? We need a quick analytics spike (Priya) to segment by OS/browser.
- Will adding more explicit error messaging create security noise (disclose less helpful info but more guidance)? Review with security.
- CI time: running the sample + embedding assert increases CI by ~4 minutes; OK for this sprint but we should avoid long-term.

Notes to self / quick commands:
- Local test script: ./dev/run-quick-lab --demo "stream-fallback" --throttle 800ms
- Revoke sandbox key: /console -> tokens -> revoke (SE demo step).

PR/Task checklist before merge:
- [ ] unit tests updated (critical path)
- [ ] e2e in sandbox passing
- [ ] short README snippet added with troubleshooting
- [ ] lab docs added and linked from quickstart landing page
- [ ] telemetry event fires in staging

Owners and pairing plan:
- Priya + Maya pair on telemetry + 401 message mapping (Wed morning pairing session).
- Ethan does readme + TLS notes, pairs with Samir on streaming demo (Thu afternoon).

Post-sprint followups (next sprint ideas):
- Add interactive quickstart (web-based sandbox that runs the 7-minute path in-page).
- Create a small "first-50-requests" billing simulator to help customers estimate cost early.
- Expand micro-labs to language-specific idioms (Ruby + Go).

Relevant links / quick references included here for rapid copy:
- Support playbook (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CS/Sandbox+Playbook
- Current quickstart landing: https://docs.redwood.ai/quickstart
- Ticket board: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/DEVEX-178

Quick retrospective note (after deploy): capture a 10-min debrief with SEs and two sample customers who recently onboarded. Record top 3 friction points and decide whether they are docs fixes vs infra work.

-- end of notebook entry --
